notes.title: Dev Log 03 - How the art is created for Astro Burn
Dev Log #01 - Why Astro Burn is created in the GDevelop Engine.
notes.notes: [h1][b]Dev log 01[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]Over the past few months, I’ve had countless friends and peers in the games industry ask me the same question — why did I choose to build Astro Burn in GDevelop instead of Unreal Engine, the tool I’ve used for most of my career?[/p][p][/p][p]In this video, I break it all down. I’ll share my reasons for switching engines, show new gameplay footage from [i]Astro Burn[/i], and give you a behind-the-scenes look at how I’m developing the game using GDevelop.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="SySQZPqwYmw;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Astro Burn early IRL Play-test at SXSW London 2025
notes.notes: [p]During the week of SXSW London, I had a few folks try out the current build of my indie game Astro Burn. This was not a formal / official play-test, but more of a “grab it and go” session to observe early first impressions.[/p][p][/p][p]What stood out?[/p][p]🔸 Players understood the story and mechanics without any instructions.[/p][p]🔸 I watched in real-time where things clicked… and where they didn’t.[/p][p]🔸 Each night, I went back and fine-tuned the game in GDevelop based on their constructive feedback.[/p][p][/p][p]Seeing people experience your game for the first time is both nerve-wracking and incredibly rewarding. [/p][p][/p][p]Check out the video below:[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="8S4ttJKzUSQ;full"][/previewyoutube]
